## 固定收益開篇論點

美國市場在勞動節假期後重新開市，美債承受的新一波壓力來自油價，而非實質殖利率。中東能源基礎設施再遭攻擊後，布蘭特原油上漲3.33%至每桶$99.49，WTI上漲3.18%至$94.39。10年期美債損益兩平通膨率上升2.2個基點至2.375%，10年期實質殖利率反而下降1.5個基點至2.415%，顯示當日市場擔憂集中於能源通膨補償，而非實質借貸成本進一步上升。

名目公債的跌勢不大，壓力主要集中在較短天期。2年期殖利率上升2.8個基點至4.395%，5年期上升1.8個基點至4.564%，10年期上升0.7個基點至4.79%，30年期則微升0.2個基點至5.246%。2年與10年期利差收窄2.1個基點至39.5個基點，2年與30年期利差收窄2.6個基點至85.1個基點。投資人因燃料漲價而提高對近期政策風險的定價，卻未在長端加入同等幅度的額外溢價。

在多座沙烏地阿拉伯能源設施遭攻擊並停止運作後，又有報導指出美軍攻擊伊朗哈爾克島與賈斯克港附近目標。布蘭特原油先在約$98結算，之後續漲；標普500指數下跌0.58%，道瓊工業平均指數下跌1.2%。貨幣市場認為聯準會9月升息的機率超過50%。週五公布的消費者物價仍是主要既定考驗，但本交易日已顯示，通往數據發布日的市場路徑可能受實體能源供應中斷改寫，而不只取決於美國國內數據。

當日美國數據也未呈現單一方向的需求訊號。小型企業樂觀程度低於預期，紐約聯準銀行調查受訪者對失業、重新找到工作、家庭財務及信貸取得更加憂慮；通膨預期則維持高檔且大致穩定。7月消費者信用增幅高於預期，二手車價格持續下跌，但月減幅放緩。聯準會面對的是近期能源壓力增強與家庭信心轉弱並存，而不是基礎需求明確加速或退潮。

即使存在上述不確定性，信用市場仍保持暢通。18家美國投資級發行人籌得$386億；雖然假期後市場重啟速度慢於近年，當日仍是2026年第三繁忙的發債日。投資級債利差小幅收窄，高收益債與硬通貨新興市場債利差大致持平。貸款借款人也大舉回歸，一方面爭取降低利差，另一方面募集收購融資。投資人願意承接新債，但龐大的供給管線與較高的基準殖利率，愈來愈明顯地決定哪些發行人能改善條件，哪些仍須出售資產、延長到期日或向債權人爭取讓步。

日本則為全球存續期部位帶來另一項挑戰。7月薪資創1997年以來最快增速，第2季GDP上修；市場準備迎接普遍預期的日本央行升息，日圓一度升向每美元153.5日圓。不過，日本家庭支出仍弱，5年期公債標售需求僅屬平淡；即使10年期JGB殖利率接近3%，機構投資人也尚未如市場有時預測般展開大規模資金回流。政策轉向確實存在，但推進速度及其對國際資金流動的影響仍未明朗。

## 能源壓力傳至美債前端

新一波油價上漲改變的主要是美債走勢的組成，而非整體幅度。10年期名目殖利率收盤僅上升0.7個基點，但其中損益兩平通膨率上升2.2個基點，實質殖利率則下跌。過去一個月，10年期損益兩平通膨率已上升12.1個基點，實質殖利率僅升2.3個基點。先前長期殖利率走高較多由實質利率、名目成長及政府供給推動；最新一個交易日則再次凸顯燃料價格與預期通膨的重要性。

能源面的消息十分具體。沙烏地阿拉伯南部多座設施遇襲並發生火災與人員受傷後停止運作。美軍攻擊伊朗主要出口樞紐哈爾克島與賈斯克附近的目標；伊朗國營電視台則播出警告，要求科威特與巴林碼頭附近的油輪人員棄船。衝突原已嚴重限制荷莫茲海峽通行，新一輪針對生產及航運基礎設施的攻擊，使原油即使在個別設施恢復運作後仍維持高檔的風險升高。

這項變化直接影響聯準會決策。政策原已在強勁就業與通膨尚未完全降溫之間權衡；8月就業報告顯示非農就業增加16.2萬人，先前月份數據上修，招聘範圍也更加廣泛，因此勞動市場疲弱已不再是避免緊縮的迫切理由。週二油價上漲，又使聯準會更難僅憑薪資增速放緩便認定通膨壓力將持續消退。美債前端因而比長端承受更大賣壓；不過，日圓在政策預期推動下上漲，其影響超過美國短率變動，美元指數仍下跌0.36%至98.808。

紐約聯準銀行8月消費者預期調查說明，能源成本上升並不會自動轉化為更強的家庭需求。1年期通膨預期維持3.6%，5年期維持3.0%，3年期則由3.3%降至3.2%；受訪者仍預期未來一年汽油價格增速將加快。

勞動與財務面的預期惡化更為顯著。受訪者對一年後失業率的預期升至2020年4月以來最高，且各年齡、所得與教育程度族群均有所上升。他們認為自己失去工作的機率下降，卻也下調非自願失業後找到新工作的可能性。對目前及未來家庭財務的評估轉弱，對當前及未來信貸取得情況的看法也同步惡化。

調查呈現的家庭並不認為通膨預期將失去控制，但對就業與資產負債表的安全感下降。這是評估油價衝擊時的重要限制：燃料漲價可以同時推高整體通膨並削弱實質購買力。聯準會目標利率區間為3.50%至3.75%；即使成長前景變得較不利，調查結果仍未讓決策官員有充分理由認為偏高的家庭通膨預期已經消除。

小型企業也提供類似警訊。NFIB小型企業樂觀指數由7月的99.8降至8月的98.7，低於市場共識99.3。這項數據不足以抵銷先前就業報告的強勢，卻顯示在融資成本與投入價格仍高之際，信心並未全面改善。

二手車價格則提供較有限的通膨抵銷。8月價格下跌0.9%，7月曾下降1.4%；年增率由1.3%降至0.4%。該類別以月率計仍具通縮作用，但跌幅縮小限制了改善程度。

家庭借款表現比信心數據所暗示的更強。7月消費者信用增加$180.6億，高於$117億的市場共識，也高於6月上修後的$145.6億增幅。信用成長可以支撐消費，但在家庭財務評估轉弱之際，也使償債成本與再融資管道更受關注。

美債供給也使市場焦點進一步集中於前端。3年期公債標售殖利率為4.474%，高於前次的4.291%。由於未提供發行前交易殖利率或投資人配售數據，這一結果確立了較高的融資水準，卻無法判斷需求品質。3個月期國庫券以3.800%得標，6個月期為3.890%，6週期為3.740%；這些結果未顯示明顯的融資失序，不足以改變市場敘事主軸，焦點仍在附息債殖利率曲線。

風險資產將能源衝擊視為一項約束，而非引發全面清算。標普500指數下跌0.58%，那斯達克100指數僅跌0.12%，費城半導體指數反而上漲1.30%。VIX上升2.75%至15.72，仍處於受控制的水準。短期殖利率上升的影響超過美元走弱，黃金期貨下跌0.64%至$4,401.50；整體信用市場定價仍有秩序。

這份韌性使投資人面臨熟悉但更加尖銳的估值矛盾。10年期美債殖利率已接近4.8%，長期實質利率仍高於2.4%，投資級債利差卻仍接近歷史低位。偏高的總殖利率繼續吸引買盤，但若能源成本、再融資負擔或需求轉弱開始損害獲利，狹窄的利差能提供的保護有限。

## 日本薪資震撼強化漸進升息理由

美國以外最清楚的新政策證據來自日本。7月名目薪資年增4.7%，高於6月上修後的4.0%及經濟學家預測的3.8%，創1997年以來最大增幅。薪資增幅已連續6個月超過3%，是34年來最長的一段期間。

數據組成進一步強化這項訊號。以排除租金的通膨調整後，實質薪資成長2.4%，為約5年來最大增幅；基本薪資增加4.1%。針對全職員工、排除獎金、加班費及抽樣偏差的指標則成長2.7%。由日本勞動組合總聯合會代表的企業員工已連續第三年取得超過5%的加薪；全國最低工資平均升至每小時¥1,177，增幅為有紀錄以來第二高。

第2季GDP也獲得上修。經濟較前季折合年率成長1.4%，高於初估的1.1%，但仍低於1.8%的市場共識。企業固定投資降幅較小是上修主因：資本支出下降0.9%，而非原先估計的1.2%。政府支出與貿易提供最大正貢獻，名目GDP折合年率成長5.5%。

這些數據使日本央行幾乎沒有理由放棄市場普遍預期的行動，即在9月17日至18日會議升息25個基點至1.25%。8月銀行放款年增5.4%，官員估計中性政策利率區間約為1.1%至2.5%。此前5次升息既未造成信用短缺，也未阻止經濟以高於潛在水準的速度成長。

然而，數據仍無法確定9月之後的升息步調。第2季消費支出持平，7月家庭支出已連續第8個月下滑。部分疲弱源於免費學校午餐上路，使帳面支出由家庭轉移至政府；但多年生活成本上升，仍使消費者態度謹慎。9月預定漲價的食品及飲料接近5,000項，是一年前的3倍，部分原因包括油價、石腦油及日圓成本。

熟悉日本央行想法的人士表示，央行對9月一次升息50個基點興趣不高。近期價格壓力仍被認為足以控制，因此較適合採取每次25個基點的步伐，以免衝擊習慣低借貸成本的家庭與市場。若勞動市場、輸入性通膨及經濟活動持續提供支持，央行考慮的反而是加快升息頻率，可能約每季升息一次。總裁植田和男已強調，必須評估先前升息的累積效果。

日圓走勢同時反映政策預期與部位調整。繼隔夜上漲1.2%後，日圓一度再升0.5%至每美元153.53日圓，9月以來累計升幅接近4%。美元兌日圓跌破155後觸發停損單及選擇權相關的美元賣盤，為日本央行緊縮預期帶來的基本面支撐增添技術性動能。

日圓走強也提高了日圓融資部位大範圍平倉的風險。SMBC日興證券曾指出，美元兌日圓跌破154可能引發更多停損與利差交易平倉。不過，美日利差及日本貿易逆差仍構成反向力量；日圓空頭部位已較輕，也意味著若日本央行在這次升息後未能確認後續緊縮預期，投資人仍有重新建立這類交易的空間。

日本國內債市呈現相似張力。5年期JGB標售投標倍數為3.42倍，低於前次的4.15倍，也略低於過去12個月平均的3.44倍；尾差由0.02擴大至0.04，債券期貨一度下跌。需求僅屬溫和疲弱，但結果顯示，在利率決定及後續升息指引均可能影響殖利率曲線中段之際，投資人不願在會議前增加部位。

JGB殖利率上升也正在改變海外投資的相對報酬。日本10年期殖利率30年來首次達到3%。美元避險成本接近3%時，經避險的10年期美債換算成日圓後殖利率約為2%，比相近天期JGB低約1個百分點。

8月資金流量首次顯示海外債券需求減少，但尚非全面資金回流。日本投資人淨賣出¥1.02兆海外短期債務及¥1,430億長期外國債券，為5個月來最大的單月外國債券淨賣出。壽險公司賣出¥1,373億長期海外債券，投資信託賣出¥301億。與此同時，退休基金買進¥2.33兆外國債券，日本投資人並淨買進¥1.3兆外國股票，規模為3月以來最大。

這些差異相當重要。日本仍是美國公債最大的外國持有國，部位約$1.1兆；日本投資人持有的海外資產則接近$5兆。日本偏好改變未必需要直接清算既有部位，便足以影響全球殖利率；只要減少配置海外市場的新資金，就會削弱長期存在的一項邊際需求來源。

目前看來，機構較傾向降低避險比率，而不是積極出售外國債券。今年新海外債券投資的估計避險比率已由2024年的62%降至約40%。這項選擇保留海外曝險，卻使報酬更容易受到日圓升值侵蝕。若日圓持續上漲、投資人更相信JGB殖利率已趨穩，或政府年金投資基金調整資產配置，資金轉向日本國內債券的速度可能加快。日本厚生勞動大臣表示，GPIF仍在考慮是否需要檢討配置，目前尚未宣布任何變更。

## 全球融資成本上升，政策制約分歧

英國以一筆£42.5億、票息5.375%、2056年1月到期的公債發行，具體呈現長期主權融資成本的上升。該債券殖利率為5.8168%，是英國債務管理局1998年成立以來，公債標售或聯合承銷發行所見最高水準。定價較票息4.25%的2055年公債高0.75個基點，訂單達£872億，其中71%來自英國國內投資人。

訂單顯示，只要殖利率大幅提高，市場仍能承接長天期債券；但其成本也突顯公共財政壓力。本財政年度£2,460億公債發行計畫中，長期傳統公債占比預定低於10%。即使如此，預算責任辦公室預測本年度債務利息支出將達£1,090億，相當於公共支出的8.4%；較長期估計顯示，2030至2031年度支出將超過£1,370億。

這批新債的同一到期券曾於2025年5月以5.405%發行，當時也創下聯合承銷發行紀錄。兩次結果對照，顯示政府邊際融資成本上升之快。殖利率走高已耗用春季估算財政緩衝的大約一半，使10月28日預算案的重要性進一步提高。

英國央行總裁貝利反對將整條市場殖利率曲線視為預先確定的政策路徑。他表示，部分定價反映能源價格可能進一步上漲的風險溢價，而不是央行的基準預測。市場已反映2026年底前升息25個基點一次，2027年再升息兩次；對9月17日會議採取行動則僅給予很低的機率。

貝利認為經濟活動頗具韌性，且7月預測後的數據略強於預期。副總裁Dave Ramsden認為國內通膨壓力相對溫和；貨幣政策委員會委員Megan Greene則警告，若油價衝擊延續，通膨預期可能更具持續性。這項分歧使實際發生的國內通膨壓力與能源風險溢價之間的差別，成為下次決策的核心。

澳洲面臨類似的政策取捨，但家庭承受壓力的跡象更清楚。澳洲央行副總裁Andrew Hauser表示，若通膨強於預測，央行已準備再次升息，但否認升息已成定局。助理總裁Sarah Hunter表示，決策委員會幾乎無法容忍通膨長期高於目標；她同時提醒，每月數據波動較大，季度讀數的權重更高。

貨幣市場認為3週內升息的機率約為70%，並已完全反映11月前升息一次。若升息25個基點，現金利率將升至4.6%，為約15年來最高。澳洲央行預期通膨要到2028年初，才會回到2%至3%目標區間的中點。

緊縮威脅已傳導至信心與房地產。西太平洋銀行9月消費者信心指數下跌5.2%至84.4，其中家庭財務狀況與一年前相比的評估下降9.2%。房貸戶信心下跌14%，其對目前是否適合購買高價商品的評估下降18%。臨時燃油消費稅減免到期後，燃料價格已升破每公升A$2。

8月企業信心下降2點至-8，企業狀況下降5點至-1，是6年來首次出現負值；獲利能力下降10點。8月全國房價下跌0.9%，較3月高點低3.6%；匯豐將房價從高點至低點的預測跌幅由8%上調至13%。Hunter表示，澳洲央行未見系統性金融穩定壓力，但正監控私人信貸及住宅開發商Bathla Group破產事件。

中國外部門傳達不同訊號。8月出口年增25.0%，符合預測，並高於7月的23.9%；進口增幅由27.5%升至28.2%，但低於30%的市場共識。貿易順差由$1,125億擴大至$1,190.9億，1月至8月累計達$8,055.1億。

前8個月高科技產品出口額成長42.9%。半導體出口量僅增加4.1%，出口金額卻成長逾一倍；汽車出口量與出口值均成長超過50%。外貿強勢降低了立即進行廣泛貨幣寬鬆的壓力，但內需疲弱及房地產長期低迷，也不支持政策全面轉向緊縮。

智利則顯示，即使成長疲弱，外部能源衝擊仍能限制政策空間。8月消費者物價較7月上漲0.6%，是0.3%市場共識的兩倍，也是4月以來最大月增幅。年通膨率由3.5%加速至4.1%，超過央行3%目標上下各1個百分點容忍區間的上緣。食品與非酒精飲料上漲1.4%，交通價格上漲1.6%，13大類別中有9類走高。

在美國固定收益市場完成收盤後，智利央行一致決議連續第6次會議將政策利率維持在4.5%。官員提到中東風險加劇，也指出國內疲弱可能比預期持續更久。7月經濟活動下降1.7%，為2022年以來最大月減幅；失業率則處於2021年以來最高。這項決定旨在保留政策彈性，而不是認可近期降息：燃料價格威脅通膨，立場更鷹派的聯準會則可能推升美元，增加智利的進口成本。

## 信用市場承接龐大供給，發行人風險仍然暴露

初級市場重新開放顯示，較高的政府公債殖利率尚未關閉企業取得信用融資的管道。18家公司合計發行$386億美國投資級債。發行人數為2020年以來最少，勞動節後首個交易日的發行量也是3年來最低；但規模仍超過過去7年同日平均，並成為2026年第三繁忙的發債日。

市場起步較慢，反映的是時機與波動，而非融資需求不足。交易行銷期間股市下跌、油價上漲，促使部分公司延後發行。儘管如此，今年以來投資級債供給已達$1.53兆，比2020年同期高8.8%，人工智慧基礎設施相關借款是主要推力。交易商預計9月發行量約為$2,150億，若實現將創單月紀錄。

GSK籌得$65億，用於協助再融資收購Nuvalent所涉及的債務；瑞銀、蒙特婁銀行及一檔Ares私人信貸基金也完成發行。評級較高的美元公司債平均殖利率接近5.5%，即使利差接近數十年低位，投資人仍可取得可觀的利息收益。

利差表現顯示，市場將基準利率壓力與信用惡化區別看待。美國投資級債利差小幅收窄，高收益債利差大致持平，硬通貨新興市場債利差也變動不大。經配息調整後，投資級債基金LQD總報酬持平，HYG與JNK跌幅均低於0.1%，EMB則下跌0.12%。

若以發行人數計，歐洲市場更為繁忙。20家借款人合計籌得約€277億，為6月9日以來最活躍的一天。法國電力公司EDF發行€10億綠色混合資本債，為延長法國核反應爐使用壽命的工程籌資。認購需求超過€30億，使殖利率由初步指引接近5.75%降至5.375%；債券最早可於2031年贖回。

EDF每年為核電機組維護及延壽投入超過€50億；這些機組供應法國逾三分之二的電力。混合資本債的成本高於優先債，但評級機構可給予部分權益認定。EDF另計畫贖回2020年發行的€8.5億混合資本債，並對2021年發行的€12.5億次順位社會債券提出收購要約，因此這筆交易兼具融資與資本結構管理目的。

亞馬遜則準備對英鎊市場需求進行更大規模的測試。公司委任摩根大通、巴克萊、匯豐及NatWest安排其首筆英鎊債交易，擬議到期年限為3年、6年、12年及19年；視市場情況，最快可自9月9日起發行，目前尚未宣布金額。

隨著人工智慧支出需求增加，這項委任延續了超大型雲端服務商分散美元市場融資來源的趨勢。亞馬遜2026年已發行等值超過$920億的債券，並規畫$2,200億資本支出，其中大部分與人工智慧有關。近期科技公司交易接獲的訂單較弱、定價更寬；主要超大型雲端服務商的違約保護成本上升速度，也超過廣泛的北美企業指數。在英國政府自身30年期融資付出1998年以來最高殖利率之際，英鎊投資人又將面對一項新的長天期債券供給。

軟銀可能進行的借款帶有更明顯的信用溢價。公司高層安排於9月14日至17日在紐約與投資人會面，評估可能發行美元投機級債券的需求。這些會議並不對應某一筆確定交易，但軟銀考慮發行$100億至$200億債券，其中可能包括歐元券別。

若以這項規模發行，交易可能成為歷來最大的投機級公司債發行之一；如符合資格，也可能顯著改變高收益債指數的組成。軟銀已取得$400億過橋貸款，用於人工智慧投資；其對OpenAI的總承諾預計在10月接近$650億。彭博產業研究估計，若待完成投資由舉債支應，總債務可能由2025年3月的約$800億升至超過$1,300億。標普給予軟銀BB+評級，與亞馬遜的AA評級形成對照；新債權人可獲得的報酬與保障，因而將是任何交易的核心。

槓桿融資市場面臨更龐大的待售管線。摩根大通估計，未來數月將有超過$1,380億收購債務進入美國與歐洲投資人市場，其中歐洲接近€400億，美國約$920億，尚未計入最高可能達$800億的美國資料中心融資。美國的供給管線是2007年以來最大，歐洲則為2021年以來最大。

貸款基金強勁流入，加上擔保貸款憑證發行成長，使市場有能力吸收供給；但龐大的發行量預料將擴大受青睞與較棘手信用之間的分化。歐洲市場上，評價較佳的單B級貸款預料起始定價為Euribor加325至350個基點，並可能收窄至約300個基點；較不受歡迎的交易可能必須支付375至425個基點。

Platinum Equity收購雀巢飲用水事業一半股權，促成首批大型交易之一。銀行推出€28億、7年期槓桿貸款，其中包括等值€16億的美元定期貸款及€12億的歐元定期貸款。投資人說明會預定9月9日開始，承諾期限為9月22日。這項更名為Peranel的事業包含Perrier與S.Pellegrino品牌，先前不僅面臨消費需求疲弱，也因水處理方式受到法律與監管審查。

美國借款人也爭相為既有貸款再融資。至少18筆貸款交易啟動，為5月18日以來最多，其中7筆為重新定價。Global Medical Response希望將一筆$29億貸款的利差由325個基點降至275至300個基點；Heartland Dental則希望將$25億債務的利差調降50個基點。這些交易顯示，即使美債殖利率推升整體負債成本，投資人需求仍能壓低信用利差。

有利的市場技術面無法解決槓桿過高或近期現金不足的借款人問題。Sophos再次嘗試延長一筆2027年3月到期、規模$21億的貸款，這是公司最迫切的到期債務。Thoma Bravo安排9月10日召開貸款人會議，承諾期限為9月22日。多家私人信貸業者此前即使獲得大幅提高殖利率的條件，仍拒絕展期。新方案可能納入更高票息、分期攤還及更嚴格的契約條款。Thoma Bravo未來數年約有$90億軟體業債務到期，貸款人正同時審視高槓桿及人工智慧可能造成的衝擊。

菲律賓的Vista Land面臨直接資金缺口。這家開發商正評估銀行融資、資本市場、營運現金及資產出售等管道，以履行包括2027年7月到期、規模$4.2億債券在內的義務。公司考慮出售兩座購物中心，價格最高可達150億披索，約合$2.4億。

其票息7.25%的2027年債券已由6月低點每$1面額47.5美分回升至約80.3美分；票息9.375%、2029年到期的債券則由5月低點33.9美分升至61.9美分。價格回升反映市場對籌資前景改善的預期，而非融資已經完成。Vista另有$4.5億債務於2029年7月到期，並須在2026年剩餘期間償還或再融資122億披索本地債券。CreditSights認為至2027年的境內到期債務大致可以處理，但境外債務能否再融資，取決於銀行承作意願及資產成功出售；若兩者均未實現，可能導致債務重整。

塞內加爾的債務處理，已由廣泛宣布逐步形成談判立場。總理Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo向國會議員表示，政府將尋求重新安排債務條件，而非債務重整；其目標是在不直接削減本金的情況下延長到期日並降低利率。債權人仍對這項區分有異議：若最終條款造成損失，採用何種名稱並不能改變其經濟結果。

投資人估計，若處理程度較深，債券回收價值約為每$1面額40至45美分。Tellimer估計，溫和延長到期日可支撐債券價值落在60多美分高端至70多美分低端；若削減本金並降低票息，回收價值可能降至40多美分中段或更低。塞內加爾債券價格約為52美分，前一週一度跌破50美分。

債務處理範圍仍是關鍵。政府有意排除以非洲金融共同體法郎計價的債務，可能迫使約$50億國際債券承擔更大調整。先前未揭露的借款，使公共債務在2024年升至GDP的130%以上；國內積欠款項總計1.96兆非洲金融共同體法郎，涉及5,425名債權人。一項$22億IMF延長信貸機制已達成工作人員層級協議，但仍須理事會批准，且債務可持續性必須取得進展。

塞內加爾表示將繼續償付債券，包括9月13日到期的2048年債券票息$3,370萬。標普已將該主權評級降至CC，並表示困境債務交換將構成違約。完成付款可維持近期的流動性履約紀錄，卻無法解決債權人待遇可比性、最終回收價值，以及國內與境外債權如何分攤損失等問題。

信實工業位於新興市場融資能力較強的一端。公司計畫透過5年期AAA債券籌集最高1,250億盧比，票息7.47%；這是其自2023年11月以來首次發債，也可能成為本年度印度規模最大的上市債券交易。基本發行規模為1,000億盧比，另設250億盧比超額配售額度。

擬議票息低於同類最高評級5年期公司債7.87%的平均殖利率，反映信實工業的信用地位。與此同時，印度企業日益偏好銀行貸款：國內公司債發行量較一年前下降約11%至8.9兆盧比，而截至7月的12個月內，新核准銀行貸款的平均利率下降29個基點。在印度央行可能進入升息循環之前，這筆交易將檢驗頂級借款人能否重新設定本地債券市場的定價基準。

## 前瞻市場意義

美國下一項考驗將美債市場結構與長天期供給結合在一起。美國財政部預計於9月9日宣布，9月10日將回購多少尚未到期的10年至20年期債券。財政部8月承諾，金額至少是先前$20億上限的兩倍，意味著不低於$40億；但財政部長Scott Bessent將此計畫形容為替債市「退燒」，促使市場期待更大規模的操作。

Wrightson ICAP的Lou Crandall認為$50億至$60億屬合理範圍；摩根士丹利估計，融資限制可能使每次操作的實際上限約為$100億。若結果接近最低承諾，可能令期待財政部採取更積極做法的投資人失望。金額若大幅提高，則可能為後續操作建立成本高昂的先例，並引發財政部是否會透過增加國庫券發行或降低現金餘額來支應回購的疑問。回購可以改變舊券的流動性與相對供給，卻不能消除政府本身的融資需求。

回購公告將在9月9日10年期公債標售前數小時公布；此前3年期公債以4.474%標售，10年期前次標售殖利率為4.683%。9月10日另有30年期公債標售，前次結果為5.216%。在企業發債量創紀錄之際，這些標售將檢驗接近4.79%及5.25%的殖利率是否足以吸收政府長天期債券。需求品質應待相關標售指標公布後再行判斷，不能只看得標殖利率。

8月生產者物價與每週初領失業救濟金人數將於9月10日美東時間上午8時30分公布。整體PPI預計月增0.4%，前值為持平；核心PPI預計由0.2%加速至0.3%。整體PPI年增率預計由4.7%升至5.3%，核心年增率則由4.2%升至4.6%。排除食品、能源與貿易的指標預計月增0.3%，年增率則由4.7%放緩至4.4%。

初領失業救濟金人數預計約20.5萬，前值為20.6萬；續領人數預計為179萬，前值177.9萬。就業報告顯示招聘範圍廣泛，偏低的申領人數將進一步強化這項訊號。若裁員顯著增加，聯準會則有理由更加重視紐約聯準銀行調查所呈現的家庭狀況惡化。

CPI將於9月11日公布。整體通膨月增率預計由0.1%加速至0.4%，年增率維持3.4%；核心價格預計月增0.2%，年增率由2.5%放緩至2.4%。若核心數據保持溫和，將支持油價主要造成整體通膨與所得衝擊的看法；若價格上漲範圍擴大，則會強化聯準會需要在9月15日至16日會議採取行動的理由。即使單月核心通膨溫和，原油若繼續上漲，政策辯論仍可能維持鷹派。

歐洲央行將在9月10日、早於上述美國數據公布前做出決策。市場預期升息25個基點，但更重要的問題是：天然氣與油價提高通膨風險之際，官員是否會確認年底前再度升息的市場預期。英國央行9月17日會議的考驗不同：貝利主張英國公債曲線部分走勢反映能源風險溢價；Greene則認為，長期油價衝擊可能使通膨預期更加持久。

日本9月17日至18日會議的重點，主要是預期升息25個基點至1.25%後的政策速度。強勁薪資、上修GDP及銀行放款支持採取行動；消費持平與家庭支出疲弱，則支持漸進升息。若指引符合約每季升息一次的路徑，將印證部分日圓漲勢，也會提高日本機構將更多資金轉投國內債券的可能性。若只有例行升息，卻未支持更快的後續步調，部分空頭回補行情可能反轉。

初級市場交易結果將顯示，信用需求能否經受本週主權債與通膨考驗。亞馬遜最快可自9月9日起發行首筆英鎊債；軟銀則自9月14日起展開非交易型投資人會議。兩者差別相當重要：亞馬遜已提出到期年限，但未公布發行額；軟銀尚未承諾進行任何發行。實際規模、利差及訂單品質，將顯示不同幣別與評級的人工智慧相關借款人還有多少融資空間。

多家財務承壓的發行人則面對更嚴格的期限。塞內加爾須於9月13日支付票息，這將檢驗其在尋求重新安排債務條件、等待IMF理事會批准期間維持償債的承諾。Sophos貸款人須在9月22日前決定，更高報酬與更強保障是否足以支持延長2027年3月到期債務。Vista Land則必須在2027年境外債務到期前，將擬議資產出售及其他融資方案轉化為現金。市場普遍暢通可以為這些發行人提供選項，但只有完成交易並與債權人議定條款，才能真正填補資金缺口。

long_thesis.english_markdown:
## Opening Fixed-Income Thesis

Oil, rather than real yields, supplied the fresh pressure on Treasuries as U.S. markets reopened after Labor Day. Brent climbed 3.33% to $99.49 a barrel and WTI rose 3.18% to $94.39 after renewed attacks on Middle Eastern energy infrastructure. The 10-year Treasury breakeven increased 2.2 basis points to 2.375%, while the 10-year real yield declined 1.5 basis points to 2.415%. That division placed the day’s inflation concern in energy compensation rather than a further increase in real borrowing costs.

The nominal selloff was modest but concentrated toward shorter maturities. The 2-year yield rose 2.8 basis points to 4.395%, the 5-year gained 1.8 basis points to 4.564%, the 10-year added 0.7 basis point to 4.79%, and the 30-year edged 0.2 basis point higher to 5.246%. The 2s10s curve flattened 2.1 basis points to 39.5 basis points, and 2s30s narrowed 2.6 basis points to 85.1. Investors raised the immediate policy risk from dearer fuel without imposing an equally large additional premium on the long end.

Reports of U.S. strikes near Iran’s Kharg Island and the port of Jask followed attacks that halted operations at several Saudi energy facilities. Brent settled around $98 before continuing higher, while the S&P 500 fell 0.58% and the Dow Jones Industrial Average lost 1.2%. Money markets assigned more than a 50% probability to a Federal Reserve increase in September. Friday’s consumer-price report remained the main scheduled test, but the session showed that the path into it could be altered by physical energy disruption rather than domestic data alone.

The day’s U.S. releases did not present a simple demand story. Small-business optimism fell below expectations, and New York Fed respondents became more concerned about unemployment, finding new work, household finances and credit access. Inflation expectations, however, remained high and broadly stable. July consumer credit increased more than forecast, while used-car prices continued to decline but at a slower monthly pace. The combination left the Fed facing firmer near-term energy pressure alongside softer household confidence, rather than a clean acceleration or retreat in underlying demand.

Credit markets remained open through that uncertainty. Eighteen U.S. investment-grade issuers raised $38.6 billion, making the session the third-busiest issuance day of 2026 even though the post-holiday reopening was slower than in recent years. Investment-grade spreads tightened modestly, while high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads were little changed. Loan borrowers also returned in force, seeking both cheaper margins and acquisition financing. Investors were willing to absorb new paper, but the large supply pipeline and higher benchmark yields increasingly determined which issuers could improve terms and which still needed asset sales, maturity extensions or creditor concessions.

Japan added a separate challenge for global duration. July wages grew at their fastest pace since 1997, second-quarter GDP was revised higher, and the yen strengthened toward 153.5 per dollar as markets prepared for a widely expected Bank of Japan increase. Yet Japanese household spending remained weak, a 5-year government-bond auction drew only muted demand, and institutions had not begun the large repatriation sometimes predicted from 10-year JGB yields near 3%. The policy shift was real; the speed and international flow consequences remained unsettled.

## Energy Pressure Reaches the Treasury Front End

The renewed oil advance changed the composition of the Treasury move more than its overall size. The 10-year nominal yield finished only 0.7 basis point higher, but its breakeven component rose 2.2 basis points as the real yield fell. Over one month, the 10-year breakeven had increased 12.1 basis points, compared with a 2.3-basis-point rise in the real yield. The latest session reinforced the importance of fuel and expected inflation after the earlier rise in long-term yields had been driven more heavily by real rates, nominal growth and government supply.

The immediate energy news was concrete. Saudi Arabia halted operations at several facilities in the south after attacks that caused fires and injuries. U.S. forces struck targets near Kharg Island, a major Iranian export hub, and Jask, while Iran’s state television carried a warning for tanker crews near Kuwaiti and Bahraini piers to abandon their vessels. The conflict had already severely constrained the Strait of Hormuz; another round of attacks on production and shipping infrastructure increased the risk that crude would remain elevated even if individual facilities returned to service.

That mattered for a Fed decision already balanced between strong employment and incomplete disinflation. The August jobs report had shown payrolls rising 162,000, upward revisions to earlier months and broader hiring, removing labor weakness as an immediate reason to avoid tightening. On Tuesday, oil provided a fresh obstacle to relying on slower wage growth as evidence that inflation pressure would continue easing. The front end accordingly sold off more than the long end, and the Dollar Index still declined 0.36% to 98.808 as the yen’s policy-driven rally outweighed the shift in U.S. short rates.

The New York Fed’s August Survey of Consumer Expectations showed why higher energy costs do not translate mechanically into stronger household demand. One-year inflation expectations held at 3.6% and 5-year expectations stayed at 3.0%, while the 3-year measure eased to 3.2% from 3.3%. Respondents nevertheless expected faster gasoline-price growth over the coming year.

Labor and financial expectations deteriorated more noticeably. The expected unemployment rate one year ahead rose to its highest since April 2020, with the increase extending across age, income and education groups. The perceived probability of losing a job declined, but respondents also marked down the likelihood of finding new work after an involuntary job loss. Assessments of present and future household finances weakened, as did views of current and prospective credit access.

The results described households that did not expect inflation to become unanchored but felt less secure about employment and balance sheets. That is an important qualification to the oil shock: fuel can raise headline inflation and reduce real purchasing power at the same time. The Fed’s target range was 3.50%-3.75%, and the survey gave policymakers little reason to treat elevated household inflation expectations as resolved even as the growth implications became less favorable.

Small businesses offered a similar caution. The NFIB Business Optimism Index fell to 98.7 in August from 99.8, below the 99.3 consensus. The release did not outweigh the preceding payroll strength, but it showed that confidence was not improving uniformly as financing costs and input prices remained elevated.

Used-car prices supplied a narrower inflation offset. They declined 0.9% in August after falling 1.4% in July, leaving prices 0.4% higher than a year earlier, down from 1.3% annual growth. The category was still disinflationary on the month, though the slower decline limited the improvement.

Household borrowing remained stronger than those confidence readings might suggest. Consumer credit increased by $18.06 billion in July, above the $11.7 billion consensus and the revised $14.56 billion June gain. Credit growth can support consumption, but in an environment of weaker household financial assessments it also places more attention on debt-service costs and the availability of refinancing.

Treasury supply reinforced the focus on the front end. The 3-year note auction stopped at 4.474%, compared with 4.291% at the previous sale. No when-issued reference or investor-allotment figures were supplied, so the yield established a higher funding level without resolving the quality of demand. The 3-month bill auction cleared at 3.800%, the 6-month at 3.890%, and the 6-week at 3.740%, but those results showed no obvious funding dislocation requiring the bills to displace the coupon curve in the market narrative.

Risk assets treated the energy shock as a constraint rather than a generalized liquidation. The S&P 500 fell 0.58%, while the Nasdaq 100 declined only 0.12% and the Philadelphia Semiconductor Index gained 1.30%. The VIX rose 2.75% to 15.72, still a contained level. Gold futures declined 0.64% to $4,401.50 as higher short-term yields outweighed the weaker dollar, while broad credit pricing remained orderly.

The resilience left investors confronting a familiar but sharper valuation tension. Investment-grade spreads remained near historically tight levels even as the 10-year Treasury yield approached 4.8% and long-term real rates stayed above 2.4%. The high all-in yield continued to attract buyers, but tight spreads offered limited protection if energy costs, refinancing burdens or weaker demand began to impair earnings.

## Japan’s Wage Shock Strengthens the Case for Incremental Tightening

Japan delivered the clearest new policy evidence outside the United States. Nominal wages rose 4.7% from a year earlier in July, accelerating from a revised 4.0% in June and exceeding the 3.8% economist forecast. It was the largest increase since 1997 and the sixth consecutive month with wage growth above 3%, the longest such run in 34 years.

The composition strengthened the signal. Real wages adjusted for inflation excluding rents rose 2.4%, the largest gain in about five years. Base pay increased 4.1%, while a measure excluding bonuses, overtime and sampling distortions rose 2.7% for full-time employees. Workers at companies represented by the Rengo labor federation had secured wage increases above 5% for a third year, and the national minimum wage rose to an average ¥1,177 an hour in the second-largest increase on record.

Second-quarter GDP was also revised higher. The economy expanded at a 1.4% annualized rate from the previous quarter, up from the initial 1.1% estimate, though below the 1.8% consensus. A smaller decline in business fixed investment accounted for the revision: capital spending fell 0.9% rather than the previously estimated 1.2%. Government expenditure and trade made the largest positive contributions, and nominal GDP grew at a 5.5% annualized pace.

The combination gave the BOJ little reason to abandon a widely expected 25-basis-point increase to 1.25% at its Sept. 17-18 meeting. Bank lending rose 5.4% from a year earlier in August, and officials estimated the neutral policy-rate range at roughly 1.1%-2.5%. Five previous increases had not produced a shortage of credit or prevented above-potential growth.

It did not, however, settle the pace after September. Consumer spending was flat in Q2, and household outlays fell for an eighth month in July. Some of the weakness reflected the introduction of free school lunches, which shifted recorded expenditure from households to government, but years of higher living costs still left consumers cautious. Nearly 5,000 food and beverage products were scheduled for price increases in September, three times the number a year earlier, partly because of oil, naphtha and yen costs.

People familiar with BOJ thinking indicated little appetite for a 50-basis-point September increase. Near-term price pressure was considered contained enough to favor quarter-point steps, avoiding a shock to households and markets accustomed to low borrowing costs. The bank was instead considering a faster cadence, potentially raising rates about once a quarter if the labor market, imported inflation and economic activity continued to justify it. Governor Kazuo Ueda had emphasized the need to assess the cumulative effect of earlier increases.

The yen reflected both that policy expectation and a positioning adjustment. It strengthened as much as 0.5% to 153.53 per dollar after gaining 1.2% overnight, taking its September advance to almost 4%. The break through 155 triggered stop-loss orders and options-related dollar selling, adding technical momentum to the fundamental support from expected BOJ tightening.

The move also raised the risk of a broader unwind in yen-funded positions. A decline below 154 had been identified by SMBC Nikko as a level that could prompt more stop-losses and carry liquidation. Yet the interest-rate gap with the United States and Japan’s trade deficit remained counterweights, and lighter short-yen positioning created room for investors to rebuild such trades if the BOJ failed to validate expectations beyond the first increase.

The domestic bond market showed similar tension. The 5-year JGB auction achieved a bid-to-cover ratio of 3.42, down from 4.15 at the previous sale and just below the 12-month average of 3.44. The tail widened to 0.04 from 0.02, and bond futures briefly declined. Demand was only modestly weak, but the result showed investors were reluctant to add exposure ahead of a meeting where both the rate decision and guidance on subsequent increases could move the belly of the curve.

Higher JGB yields are also changing the relative economics of overseas investment. Japan’s 10-year yield had reached 3% for the first time in three decades. With dollar-hedging costs near 3%, a hedged 10-year Treasury yielded about 2% in yen terms, roughly 1 percentage point less than a comparable JGB.

August flow data offered the first signs of reduced foreign-bond appetite, though not a wholesale repatriation. Japanese investors sold a net ¥1.02 trillion of overseas short-term debt and ¥143 billion of long-term foreign bonds, the largest monthly net sale of foreign bonds in five months. Life insurers sold ¥137.3 billion of long-term overseas bonds and investment trusts sold ¥30.1 billion. At the same time, pension funds bought ¥2.33 trillion of foreign bonds, and Japanese investors purchased a net ¥1.3 trillion of foreign equities, the largest amount since March.

Those differences matter because Japan remains the largest foreign holder of U.S. Treasuries, with roughly $1.1 trillion, and Japanese investors own almost $5 trillion of overseas assets. Global yields do not require outright liquidation to feel the effect of changing Japanese preferences. Directing less new money abroad would remove a long-standing source of marginal demand.

For now, institutions appeared more inclined to reduce hedges than to sell foreign bonds aggressively. The estimated hedge ratio on new overseas bond investment had declined to roughly 40% this year from 62% in 2024. That choice preserves foreign exposure but makes returns more vulnerable to yen appreciation. A sustained currency rally, greater confidence that JGB yields were stabilizing, or a change in the Government Pension Investment Fund’s allocation could accelerate the shift toward domestic duration. Japan’s health minister said the GPIF was still considering whether an allocation review was needed; no change had been announced.

## Higher Global Funding Costs Meet Divergent Policy Constraints

Britain crystallized the rise in long-term sovereign funding costs with a £4.25 billion sale of 5.375% January 2056 gilts at a 5.8168% yield, the highest recorded at a gilt auction or syndication since the Debt Management Office was established in 1998. The transaction priced 0.75 basis point above the 4.25% 2055 gilt and attracted £87.2 billion of orders, 71% from domestic investors.

The order book showed that duration could still be placed at substantially higher yields, but the cost underscored the pressure on the public finances. Long-dated conventional debt is scheduled to account for less than 10% of the £246 billion gilt program for the fiscal year. Even so, the Office for Budget Responsibility had forecast £109 billion of debt-interest expense this year, equal to 8.4% of public spending, while longer-run projections put the bill above £137 billion by 2030-31.

The new bond followed an earlier sale of the same maturity in May 2025 at 5.405%, itself a syndication record at the time. The contrast shows how quickly the government’s marginal cost has risen. Higher yields had already consumed roughly half of the fiscal buffer calculated in the spring, increasing the stakes for the Oct. 28 budget.

Bank of England Governor Andrew Bailey pushed back against treating the entire market curve as a predetermined policy path. He said part of the pricing reflected a risk premium for further energy-price increases rather than the central bank’s central forecast. Markets had priced one 25-basis-point increase by the end of 2026 and two more in 2027, while assigning only a slim probability to action at the Sept. 17 meeting.

Bailey described activity as reasonably resilient and said data since the July forecast had been slightly stronger than expected. Deputy Governor Dave Ramsden judged domestic inflation pressure relatively benign, while Monetary Policy Committee member Megan Greene warned that a prolonged oil shock could make inflation expectations more persistent. The disagreement placed the distinction between realized domestic pressure and energy insurance at the center of the next decision.

Australia faced a similar policy trade-off with clearer signs of household strain. Deputy Governor Andrew Hauser said the Reserve Bank was prepared to raise rates again if inflation proved stronger than forecast but denied that another increase was inevitable. Assistant Governor Sarah Hunter said the board had little tolerance for inflation remaining above target for an extended period, while cautioning that monthly data were volatile and quarterly readings carried more weight.

Money markets assigned about a 70% probability to an increase within three weeks and fully priced one by November. A quarter-point move would lift the cash rate to 4.6%, its highest in about 15 years. The RBA expected inflation to return to the midpoint of its 2%-3% target only in early 2028.

The tightening threat was already reaching confidence and property. Westpac’s consumer-sentiment index fell 5.2% to 84.4 in September, with assessments of family finances compared with a year earlier down 9.2%. Sentiment among mortgage holders dropped 14%, while their assessment of whether it was a good time to buy a major item fell 18%. Fuel prices had risen above A$2 a liter after the expiration of a temporary excise-tax reduction.

Business confidence declined 2 points to -8 in August, while conditions fell 5 points to -1, the first negative reading in six years. Profitability dropped 10 points. National home prices fell 0.9% in August and were 3.6% below their March peak; HSBC increased its forecast peak-to-trough decline to 13% from 8%. Hunter said the RBA saw no systemic financial-stability stress but was monitoring private credit and the insolvency of residential developer Bathla Group.

China’s external sector provided a different signal. Exports rose 25.0% from a year earlier in August, matching forecasts and accelerating from 23.9% in July. Imports increased 28.2%, up from 27.5% but below the 30% consensus. The trade surplus widened to $119.09 billion from $112.5 billion, taking the January-August total to $805.51 billion.

High-technology exports rose 42.9% in value during the first eight months. Semiconductor export values more than doubled even though volumes increased only 4.1%, and vehicle exports rose more than 50% in both volume and value. The strength reduced the immediate pressure for broad monetary easing, even as weak domestic demand and a persistent property slump argued against an outright tightening turn.

Chile demonstrated how an external energy shock can constrain policy despite weak growth. August consumer prices rose 0.6% from July, twice the 0.3% consensus and the fastest monthly increase since April. Annual inflation accelerated to 4.1% from 3.5%, moving above the upper edge of the central bank’s 3% target plus-or-minus 1 percentage point tolerance range. Food and non-alcoholic beverages rose 1.4%, transportation increased 1.6%, and nine of 13 categories advanced.

In a later development after the completed U.S. fixed-income close, Chile’s central bank unanimously kept its policy rate at 4.5% for a sixth meeting. Officials cited intensified Middle East risks alongside the possibility that domestic weakness would persist longer than expected. Economic activity had fallen 1.7% in July, the largest monthly decline since 2022, and unemployment was at its highest since 2021. The decision preserved flexibility rather than endorsing near-term easing: fuel prices threatened inflation, while a more hawkish Fed could strengthen the dollar and raise Chilean import costs.

## Credit Absorbs Heavy Supply but Leaves Issuer Risk Exposed

The reopening of primary markets demonstrated that higher government yields had not closed credit access. Eighteen companies sold $38.6 billion of U.S. investment-grade bonds. That was the fewest issuers since 2020 and the lowest first-post-Labor-Day volume in three years, but it still exceeded the 7-year average for the session and ranked as the third-busiest issuance day of 2026.

The slower opening reflected timing and volatility rather than a lack of financing demand. Stocks were lower and oil was higher as transactions were marketed, prompting some companies to delay. Year-to-date investment-grade supply had nevertheless reached $1.53 trillion, 8.8% above the comparable 2020 pace, with artificial-intelligence infrastructure borrowing a major contributor. Dealers expected about $215 billion for September, which would be a record for the month.

GSK raised $6.5 billion to help refinance debt associated with its acquisition of Nuvalent, while UBS, Bank of Montreal and an Ares private-credit fund also issued. Better-rated dollar corporate bonds offered average yields near 5.5%, enabling investors to earn substantial income even while spreads remained close to multidecade lows.

The spread outcome showed that the market distinguished benchmark-rate pressure from credit deterioration. U.S. investment-grade spreads tightened modestly, high-yield spreads were little changed, and hard-currency emerging-market spreads were also little changed. The LQD investment-grade fund was flat on a distribution-adjusted total-return basis, while HYG and JNK declined less than 0.1% and EMB fell 0.12%.

Europe was busier by issuer count. Twenty borrowers raised roughly €27.7 billion, the most active day since June 9. EDF sold €1 billion of green hybrid bonds to finance work extending the life of its French nuclear reactors. Demand exceeded €3 billion, allowing the yield to tighten to 5.375% from initial indications near 5.75%. The securities are first callable in 2031.

EDF spends more than €5 billion annually on maintenance and life-extension work for a nuclear fleet that supplies over two-thirds of France’s electricity. The hybrid format is more expensive than senior debt but receives partial equity treatment from rating agencies. EDF also planned to redeem €850 million of hybrids issued in 2020 and tender for €1.25 billion of subordinated social bonds sold in 2021, making the transaction part financing and part capital-structure management.

Amazon prepared a larger test of sterling demand. It mandated JPMorgan, Barclays, HSBC and NatWest for its first pound-denominated transaction, with proposed maturities of 3, 6, 12 and 19 years and a possible launch from Sept. 9, subject to market conditions. No amount had been announced.

The mandate extended hyperscalers’ diversification away from the dollar market as their AI spending requirements grew. Amazon had already sold the equivalent of more than $92 billion of bonds in 2026 and planned $220 billion of capital expenditure, most of it related to AI. Recent technology deals had drawn weaker orders and wider pricing, while default-protection costs for major hyperscalers had risen faster than a broad North American corporate index. Sterling investors were being offered another source of long duration just as the government paid a record post-1998 yield on its own 30-year financing.

SoftBank’s prospective borrowing carried a more explicit credit premium. Executives scheduled New York investor meetings for Sept. 14-17 to assess demand for possible dollar speculative-grade issuance. The meetings were not tied to a specific offering, but the company was considering $10 billion-$20 billion of bonds, potentially including a euro tranche.

At that size, the sale could become one of the largest speculative-grade corporate offerings and materially affect high-yield index composition if eligible. SoftBank had secured a $40 billion bridge loan to finance AI investments, while its total commitment to OpenAI was expected to approach $65 billion by October. Bloomberg Intelligence estimated that gross debt could rise above $130 billion from about $80 billion in March 2025 if pending investments were debt-funded. S&P rated SoftBank BB+, contrasting with Amazon’s AA rating and making the cost and protection offered to new creditors central to any transaction.

The leveraged-finance market faced an even larger queue. JPMorgan estimated more than $138 billion of buyout debt was due to reach U.S. and European investors in coming months: nearly €40 billion in Europe and about $92 billion in the United States, excluding as much as $80 billion of possible U.S. data-center financing. The U.S. pipeline was the largest since 2007, while Europe’s was the biggest since 2021.

Strong inflows into loan funds and growth in collateralized-loan-obligation issuance gave the market capacity to absorb the supply, but the volume was expected to widen the separation between favored and difficult credits. Well-regarded single-B loans in Europe were expected to begin around 325-350 basis points over Euribor and potentially tighten toward 300 basis points. Less popular transactions could require 375-425 basis points.

Platinum Equity’s purchase of half of Nestlé’s water business produced one of the first major deals. Banks launched €2.8 billion of 7-year leveraged loans, divided into a €1.6 billion-equivalent dollar term loan and a €1.2 billion euro term loan. Investor calls were due to begin Sept. 9, with commitments required by Sept. 22. The business, renamed Peranel, includes Perrier and S.Pellegrino and had faced weak consumer demand as well as legal and regulatory scrutiny over water-treatment methods.

U.S. borrowers also rushed to refinance existing loans. At least 18 loan deals launched, the most since May 18, including seven repricings. Global Medical Response sought to reduce the spread on a $2.9 billion loan to 275-300 basis points from 325 basis points, while Heartland Dental aimed to lower the margin on $2.5 billion of debt by 50 basis points. The transactions showed that investor demand could still reduce credit margins even while Treasury yields increased the total cost of debt.

That favorable technical backdrop did not resolve borrowers whose problem was leverage or near-term cash. Sophos began another attempt to extend a $2.1 billion loan due in March 2027, its most urgent maturity. Thoma Bravo scheduled a lender call for Sept. 10, with commitments due Sept. 22. Several private-credit firms had previously rejected an extension despite being offered a steep yield increase. The new proposal could include a higher coupon, amortization and tighter covenants. Thoma Bravo had roughly $9 billion of software debt maturing over the next few years, and lenders were scrutinizing both high leverage and possible AI disruption.

Vista Land faced a direct funding gap in the Philippines. The developer was evaluating bank financing, capital markets, operating cash and asset sales to meet obligations including a $420 million bond due in July 2027. It was considering selling two malls for as much as 15 billion pesos, or $240 million.

Its 7.25% 2027 bonds had recovered to about 80.3 cents from a June low of 47.5, while 9.375% notes due in 2029 rose to 61.9 cents from a May low of 33.9. The recovery reflected improving expectations for fundraising, not completed financing. Vista also had $450 million due in July 2029 and 12.2 billion pesos of local bonds to repay or refinance during the remainder of 2026. CreditSights considered onshore maturities through 2027 largely manageable but said refinancing offshore debt depended on bank appetite and successful asset disposals; failure on those fronts could lead to restructuring.

Senegal’s debt treatment moved from a broad announcement toward a negotiating position. Prime Minister Ahmadou Al Aminou Lo told lawmakers that the government would seek a reprofiling rather than a restructuring, defining its objective as longer maturities and lower interest rates without an explicit principal reduction. The distinction remained contested by creditors: if the eventual terms impose a loss, the label will not determine the economic outcome.

Investor estimates placed recoveries near 40-45 cents in a deeper treatment. Tellimer estimated that a mild maturity extension could support values in the high 60s to low 70s, while principal reductions and lower coupons could push recoveries into the mid-40s or below. Senegal’s bonds traded around 52 cents after having fallen below 50 the prior week.

The perimeter remained decisive. The government intended to exclude CFA franc-denominated debt, potentially forcing a larger adjustment onto roughly $5 billion of international bonds. Previously undisclosed borrowing had pushed public debt above 130% of GDP in 2024, and domestic arrears totaled 1.96 trillion CFA francs owed to 5,425 claimants. A $2.2 billion IMF extended-credit facility had reached staff-level agreement but still required board approval and progress toward debt sustainability.

Senegal said it would continue servicing its notes, including a $33.7 million coupon on the 2048 bond due Sept. 13. S&P had downgraded the sovereign to CC and said a distressed exchange would constitute default. Payment would preserve near-term liquidity performance, but it would not settle creditor comparability, eventual recovery values or the division of losses between domestic and external claims.

Reliance Industries occupied the stronger end of emerging-market funding. It planned to raise as much as 125 billion rupees through 5-year AAA notes at a 7.47% coupon, its first bond sale since November 2023 and potentially the largest listed Indian transaction of the year. The base size was 100 billion rupees with a 25 billion-rupee greenshoe.

The proposed coupon was below the 7.87% average yield on comparable top-rated 5-year corporate debt. That advantage reflected Reliance’s credit standing even as Indian companies increasingly favored bank loans: domestic corporate issuance had fallen about 11% from a year earlier to 8.9 trillion rupees, while the average rate on newly sanctioned bank loans declined 29 basis points in the 12 months through July. The deal would test whether a premier borrower could reset the local bond benchmark before a possible Reserve Bank of India tightening cycle.

## Forward Market Significance

The next U.S. test combines Treasury market structure with duration supply. Treasury is expected on Sept. 9 to announce the size of its Sept. 10 buyback of outstanding 10- to 20-year securities. The department committed in August to at least double the previous $2 billion maximum, implying no less than $4 billion, but Secretary Scott Bessent’s description of the program as an effort to cool a bond-market “fever” encouraged expectations of a larger operation.

Wrightson ICAP’s Lou Crandall considered $5 billion-$6 billion plausible, while Morgan Stanley estimated that funding constraints could impose a practical ceiling around $10 billion per operation. A result near the minimum could disappoint investors who had anticipated a more activist approach. A much larger amount could establish a costly precedent for later operations and raise questions about whether Treasury would fund purchases with additional bills or a lower cash balance. Buybacks can alter the liquidity and relative supply of older securities, but they do not remove the government’s underlying financing requirement.

The announcement comes hours before the Sept. 9 sale of 10-year notes, following the 3-year auction at 4.474%. The 10-year’s previous auction yield was 4.683%. A 30-year sale follows Sept. 10 after a previous 5.216% result. The auctions will test whether yields near 4.79% and 5.25% are sufficient to absorb government duration alongside record corporate borrowing. Demand should be judged from the supplied auction metrics when released, rather than from the auction yield alone.

August producer prices and weekly jobless claims arrive Sept. 10 at 8:30 a.m. ET. Headline PPI is expected to rise 0.4% after no monthly change, while core PPI is expected to increase 0.3% after 0.2%. The annual headline rate is expected to accelerate to 5.3% from 4.7%, and core inflation to 4.6% from 4.2%. The measure excluding food, energy and trade is forecast to rise 0.3% on the month and slow to 4.4% annually from 4.7%.

Initial claims are expected near 205,000 after 206,000, and continuing claims at 1.79 million after 1.779 million. The employment report showed broad hiring and low claims would reinforce that message. A material rise in layoffs would instead give the Fed a reason to weigh the household deterioration in the New York survey more heavily.

CPI follows Sept. 11. Headline inflation is expected to accelerate to 0.4% from 0.1% on the month and remain at 3.4% annually. Core prices are expected to rise 0.2% and slow to 2.4% from 2.5% year on year. A contained core result would support the view that oil is principally a headline and income shock; broader acceleration would strengthen the case that the Fed needs to respond at its Sept. 15-16 meeting. Continued crude gains could keep the policy debate hawkish even if one month of core inflation is moderate.

The European Central Bank’s Sept. 10 decision precedes those U.S. releases. Markets expect a 25-basis-point increase, but the more consequential question is whether officials validate expectations for another move by year-end as gas and oil raise inflation risks. The Bank of England’s Sept. 17 meeting presents a different test: Bailey has argued that part of the gilt curve represents an energy risk premium, while Greene sees a route through which a prolonged oil shock could make expectations more persistent.

Japan’s Sept. 17-18 meeting is largely about the pace after an expected quarter-point increase to 1.25%. Strong wages, revised GDP and bank lending support action, while flat consumption and weak household spending argue for incremental steps. Guidance consistent with roughly quarterly increases would validate part of the yen rally and increase the chance that Japanese institutions direct more capital toward domestic bonds. A routine hike without support for the faster path could reverse some short covering.

Primary-market execution will reveal whether credit demand survives the week’s sovereign and inflation tests. Amazon could launch its first sterling bonds from Sept. 9, while SoftBank begins non-deal meetings Sept. 14. The distinction is important: Amazon has proposed maturities but no amount, and SoftBank has not committed to an offering. Actual size, spreads and order quality will show how much capacity remains for AI-related borrowers across currencies and ratings.

Several stressed credits face harder deadlines. Senegal’s Sept. 13 coupon tests its pledge to maintain debt service while it pursues reprofiling and awaits IMF board approval. Sophos lenders must decide by Sept. 22 whether higher compensation and stronger protections justify extending the March 2027 maturity. Vista Land must convert proposed asset sales and financing alternatives into cash before its 2027 offshore maturity. Broadly open markets can give those issuers options, but only completed transactions and agreed creditor terms can close their funding gaps.

section_summaries.summary: U.S. investment-grade borrowers raised $38.6 billion as high all-in yields sustained demand and spreads remained orderly. Heavy corporate and leveraged-finance pipelines can still clear, but pricing power increasingly depends on credit quality: strong borrowers are refinancing or diversifying funding, while SoftBank, Sophos, Vista Land and Senegal face distinct leverage, maturity or creditor constraints that open markets alone cannot resolve.

Treasury’s buyback announcement and 10- and 30-year auctions will test duration absorption near elevated yields. U.S. PPI, jobless claims and CPI will determine whether oil remains mainly a headline and income shock or broadens into underlying inflation. BOJ guidance after an expected increase will test whether tightening can proceed about once a quarter and redirect more Japanese capital toward domestic bonds.

overall_summary.headline: Oil-driven inflation pressure pushes Treasury yields higher and flattens the curve
overall_summary.session_narrative:
Treasuries sold off modestly as renewed attacks on Middle Eastern energy infrastructure drove Brent up 3.33% to $99.49 and WTI up 3.18% to $94.39. The 2-year yield rose 2.8 basis points to 4.395%, while the 10-year added 0.7 basis point to 4.79% and the 30-year edged 0.2 basis point higher to 5.246%. The 2s10s curve flattened 2.1 basis points to 39.5 basis points.

The composition identified energy inflation, rather than higher real borrowing costs, as the fresh pressure. The 10-year breakeven rose 2.2 basis points to 2.375% while the real yield fell 1.5 basis points to 2.415%. Money markets assigned more than a 50% probability to a September Fed increase, but weaker small-business optimism and deteriorating household views of employment, finances and credit access showed that dearer fuel could raise inflation while restraining purchasing power.

Credit remained open despite the uncertainty: 18 U.S. investment-grade issuers raised $38.6 billion, investment-grade spreads tightened modestly, and high-yield and hard-currency emerging-market spreads were little changed. Japan added a separate global-duration risk as the fastest wage growth since 1997 strengthened the case for an expected BOJ increase, although weak household spending and limited evidence of wholesale foreign-bond repatriation left the pace and international effects unsettled.
